newsitem.title: LATVIA: Denmark urges EU talks with all east Europeans.
newsitem.headline: Denmark urges EU talks with all east Europeans.

text.p: Denmark wants the European Union (EU) to start entry talks with all east European candidates at the same time, Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen said in a Latvian newspaper interview published on Tuesday.
The Commission last week agreed in principle to start talks with only five states in the first phase of eastwards expansion: Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovenia and Estonia.
Latvia and Lithuania were shocked by the news only one Baltic state would be invited, as all three have been knocking long and hard on the EU's door since quitting the former Soviet Union in 1991.
But Helveg Petersen told Latvian newspaper Diena in an interview that the Commission decision was not final.
"The Danish stance since the very beginning has been very firm: talks should start with all candidate states," he said.
"We will keep to this point of view. I am sure that others will support us also," he added.
He said the Commission did not take the political decision on new EU members but that this would be done by EU governments at a meeting in Luxembourg in December.
The EU executive was due on Tuesday to confirm last week's decision and was due on Wednesday to release its opinion to member state governments on the preparedness of EU candidates.
Nordic EU members Denmark, Sweden and Finland have been strong supporters of the Balts in their EU efforts.
As well as Latvia and Lithuania, Bulgaria, Slovakia and Romania also want EU membership.
